hypothesis: Local selection mosaics rather than one universal agent determine which capitulum trait state is favoured.
causal_path: environment + spatial/population context -> interaction opportunity/reproductive assurance/enemy/abiotic exposure -> module-specific functional leverage -> pollination/protection/antagonism -> filled achenes -> recruitment
current_evidence: Interaction synthesis rejects universal pollinator or antagonist dominance and supports context dependence; reproductive antagonist cost is strong in the general literature.
main_falsifier: Trait effects are stable across contexts and a single common agent explains module fitness effects without context interaction.
next_test: Fit ancestry-aware field models with local pollinator opportunity, antagonist pressure, abiotic exposure and reproductive outcome on the same individuals.
claim_boundary: This is a causal architecture to test, not a fitted multiplicative law.

hypothesis: Capitulum orientation changes time-window pollination leverage even when all-day visitation or static preference is weak.
causal_path: orientation -> early/time-window head temperature and floral presentation -> effective contacts/pollen transfer -> filled achenes
current_evidence: External/global mechanism reduction retained timing as part of the only family matching all core calibration targets; current phylogeny requires >=5 orientation-state changes across all six accepted topologies.
main_falsifier: Sham-controlled reorientation changes neither time-resolved effective contact/pollen transfer nor filled-achene fitness across informative weather/time windows.
next_test: Within-population randomized sham vs reorientation with time-resolved visitor identity/effective contact, pollen response and filled achenes.
claim_boundary: Repeated orientation states do not identify timing as their cause.

hypothesis: Nodding/downward orientation protects reproductive function from rain/wetting and possibly UV exposure.
causal_path: orientation -> wetting/rain/UV exposure -> pollen/reproductive-organ integrity -> filled achenes
current_evidence: External Asteraceae evidence and pattern-reduction calibration support an abiotic-protection route; timing+protection jointly best matched the preregistered calibration targets.
main_falsifier: Reorientation changes exposure but not pollen integrity/seed fitness, or changes seed fitness without any preregistered protection mediator.
next_test: Pair sham/reorientation with rainfall or controlled wetting exposure, pollen viability/deposition and filled-achene endpoint.
claim_boundary: Do not interpret a fitness effect with unchanged preregistered mediators as proof of rain/UV protection; retain an unexplained ORI5 outcome.

hypothesis: Orientation can alter antagonist exposure independently of pollination and abiotic protection.
causal_path: orientation -> florivore/seed-predator discovery or access -> damage -> filled achenes
current_evidence: General reproductive antagonist pressure is strong, but focal orientation-specific antagonist evidence is not established.
main_falsifier: Orientation manipulation has no repeatable effect on antagonist access/damage while other pathways explain fitness.
next_test: Record antagonist exposure/damage on the same sham/reoriented heads without folding it into pollinator response.
claim_boundary: Antagonist pressure in Cirsium generally does not establish an orientation mechanism.

hypothesis: Flower colour has context-dependent functional effects through pollinator effective contact and/or abiotic response, rather than a universal colour preference.
causal_path: ancestry-resolved colour -> visitor guild/effective contact and/or floral abiotic response -> reproductive fitness
current_evidence: Colour is a strong visible module globally and W/C ecological contrasts are source-backed, but the macroevolutionary direction remains blocked by fixed-white sampling and rate identifiability.
main_falsifier: Within ancestry-matched, flowering-overlap contexts, colour differences do not predict effective pollination, abiotic response or reproductive fitness.
next_test: Use overlapping W/C populations with calibrated visible+UV colour, visitor/effective-contact observations and filled achenes; keep ancestry explicit.
claim_boundary: Ecological colour function can be tested before the macroevolutionary loss/regain direction is known.

hypothesis: Floral display has a local pollinator-benefit versus antagonist-cost optimum rather than a monotonic bigger-is-better effect.
causal_path: capitulum size/head number + local flowering density -> pollinator discovery/probing AND antagonist discovery -> filled achenes
current_evidence: Cirsium purpuratum and broader synthesis support simultaneous pollinator benefit and predispersal seed-predator cost with density dependence.
main_falsifier: Pollinator and antagonist responses are both monotonic in the same direction and no context-dependent fitness optimum appears.
next_test: Measure head number/size, local density, visits, heads probed, effective contacts, antagonist damage and final filled achenes on the same plants.
claim_boundary: Visitor abundance alone is not the fitness pathway.

hypothesis: Phyllary/spine architecture can reduce antagonist access at a possible cost to pollinator access.
causal_path: validated phyllary/spine architecture -> antagonist access/damage down; possible pollinator effective contact down -> net seed fitness
current_evidence: Broader Cardueae/Asteraceae evidence makes defence plausible, but current image-derived geometry is only a proxy and focal Cirsium adaptation is unproven.
main_falsifier: Direct repeatable focal morphology does not exist, or validated architecture does not affect antagonist/pollinator access or fitness.
next_test: First validate direct botanical phyllary spread/spine length/direction; manipulate only if that gate passes.
claim_boundary: Do not call 2-D image spine-like geometry a defence trait.

hypothesis: Downstream recruitment can amplify, gate or erase seed-output effects, so reproductive fitness is not the endpoint of demographic adaptation by default.
causal_path: trait -> interaction/protection -> filled achenes -> safe-site/disturbance/density-dependent recruitment
current_evidence: Meta-synthesis supports demographic gating as context dependent.
main_falsifier: Seed-output contrasts reliably predict recruitment across microsite and density contexts without additional gating.
next_test: Run recruitment microsite work only after a clear focal filled-achene contrast is demonstrated.
claim_boundary: Do not infer population growth from seed output alone.

hypothesis: Erect/upward and nodding/downward states have changed repeatedly within the shallow East Asian Cirsium radiation.
causal_path: accepted nuclear topology ensemble + conservative orientation states -> repeated state transitions
current_evidence: Post-tree preflight: all six AU-nonrejected topologies require a minimum of 5 state changes from 17 resolved taxa (U=9,D=8).
main_falsifier: Same-voucher/population validation collapses the binary state coding or expanded topology/state uncertainty reduces the lower bound to a single change.
next_test: Validate orientation on exact vouchers/populations and map those states onto the ancestry-resolved tree before naming independent adaptive transitions.
claim_boundary: Repeated state change is supported; parallel/convergent adaptation is not yet established.

hypothesis: Rapid radiation redeployed semi-independent capitulum modules across different selection mosaics (modular evolvability), versus a single shared common-lability axis.
causal_path: repeated module transitions + ancestry control + module-specific ecological fitness paths -> compare modular versus shared-latent models
current_evidence: Orientation now supplies a topology-robust repeated-state signal; colour, display and defence transition histories/function are not yet equally resolved.
main_falsifier: A shared common-lability model predicts trait/environment/fitness structure as well as or better than module-specific models out of sample.
next_test: After multiple module transition maps and focal causal results exist, compare shared-latent versus module-specific ancestry-aware models with out-of-sample prediction.
claim_boundary: Do not call modular evolvability merely because traits differ among taxa.

hypothesis: Repeated colour states may reuse standing/introgressed/regulatory anthocyanin machinery; regulatory suppression could permit re-expression more readily than structural pathway loss.
causal_path: ancestry -> coding/regulatory haplotype -> matched floral RNA -> pigment chemistry -> calibrated colour
current_evidence: General molecular literature makes both reversible regulatory suppression and structural loss plausible; East Asian directionality is not yet identified.
main_falsifier: Independent W/C systems show unrelated structural loss or no shared/reused regulatory architecture.
next_test: Only after >=2 independent W/C transitions are credible, link ancestry, candidate haplotypes, floral RNA, pigment and colour on matched individuals.
claim_boundary: Do not call C. irumtiense a molecular colour regain before transition direction and pathway evidence are established.
